narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Updated for dusk: dry conditions persist through the evening, but convective instability spikes early tonight peaking around 18:00 EAT with substantial model disagreement — UKMO surges to an extreme 6,300 J/kg CAPE and Best Match to 3,140 J/kg, while ICON (1,330 J/kg) and ECMWF (1,170 J/kg) indicate moderate instability and GFS remains low at 180 J/kg — introducing potential for isolated nocturnal thunderstorms despite zero surface rainfall forecast. Warm weather continues tomorrow with daytime maximums near 32°C / 90°F to 34°C / 93°F before rain probability increases by late Sunday.

## Today's Forecast
Warm and mostly clear conditions mark the start of dusk, with daytime highs near 34°C / 93°F cooling toward an overnight low around 20°C / 68°F. Measurable rainfall is not expected tonight (0.0 mm / 0.0 in), though sharp atmospheric instability maintains a risk of nocturnal lightning and sudden wind shifts. Peak daytime UV exposure (index 9.2) has passed. Light evening winds at 11 km/h (6 kt) from the SW will ease overnight before picking up tomorrow afternoon to 26 km/h (14 kt) from the SW with gusts up to 39 km/h (21 kt). Ground air quality sensors have no current data; the last actual reading was 57 at Dunga Beach, 3 hours ago; the model guidance says US AQI levels are around 89 (Moderate) overnight.

## Extended Outlook
For Sunday through Tuesday (Sept 6–8), daytime temperatures moderate slightly from 32°C / 90°F down to 31°C / 88°F. Rain chances re-emerge Sunday afternoon and peak on Tuesday, September 8th (Day+3), where ECMWF forecasts 4.2 mm (0.17 in) of precipitation (96% probability), ICON projects 0.9 mm (0.04 in) (68% probability), and UKMO shows 1.2 mm (0.05 in), while GFS calls for 0.6 mm (0.02 in) and Kenya Met forecasts dry conditions. Looking further into days 4–7 (Sept 9–12), unsettled weather continues across Nyanza Basin, culminating around Saturday, September 12th (Day+7), when ECMWF projects 5.0 mm (0.20 in) of rain (86% probability), Best Match projects 5.4 mm (0.21 in) (86% probability), and GFS projects 4.5 mm (0.18 in) (35% probability). Consult Day+7 track records for range guidance, where GFS currently holds 78% rain verification skill compared to 67% on ECMWF.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
No severe daytime precipitation hazards or flooding are expected across the basin tonight or tomorrow. However, convective available potential energy (CAPE) peaks early tonight around 18:00 EAT, driven by a sharp disagreement across models: UKMO predicts extreme CAPE of 6,300 J/kg, Best Match reaches 3,140 J/kg, ICON shows 1,330 J/kg, ECMWF reaches 1,170 J/kg, and GFS indicates 180 J/kg. Elevated instability over dry lower atmospheric layers can trigger isolated nocturnal lightning, thunder, and localized sudden wind gusts without generating measurable surface rain.

## Lake Victoria — Conditions for Boaters
Overnight winds on Lake Victoria will blow gently at 10 km/h (5 kt) to 18 km/h (10 kt) from the SW to W. Tomorrow, lake winds strengthen to 22 km/h (12 kt) from the SE in the morning, turning southwesterly in the afternoon at 28 km/h (15 kt) with gusts reaching 38 km/h (21 kt). Substantial nocturnal convective instability develops over the lake tonight, with CAPE exceeding 2,000–2,800 J/kg across ECMWF, UKMO, and Best Match guidance. Mariners and night boaters should prepare for sudden squalls, abrupt wind shifts, and localized lightning over open water despite dry surface precipitation forecasts.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northeast (1005 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1017 hPa) — a 12 hPa spread, a strong large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the northeast is filling over the next three days. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Locally across Nyanza Basin, mean sea-level pressure averages 1011.2 hPa today with a mild 24-hour drop (-1.1 to -1.8 hPa) before recovering slightly toward 1012–1013 hPa over the next 48 to 72 hours.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
Guidance recency floor: model data behind this update is at least 9.0 hours old (last aligned cycle 06:00Z on Sept 5).
Track record weighting and model performance: At Day+0, Best Match is the top-performing rain caller in the record (84% accuracy) and GFS the weakest (64%). GFS systematically over-forecasts peak surface wind speeds by +21.4 km/h at Day+0, +18.5 km/h at Day+3, and +23.3 km/h at Day+7, so its wind forecasts are discounted in favor of ECMWF (+9.8 km/h error) and ICON (+8.6 km/h error). ICON systematically over-forecasts overnight low temperatures (-2.4°C error at Day+0, -2.8°C at Day+3), while UKMO systematically under-forecasts overnight lows (+1.5°C error at Day+0, +1.9°C at Day+3). At Day+3, Best Match leads rain verification (86%) while ICON is weakest (68%). At Day+7, GFS leads rain verification (78%).
Local met service evaluation: The Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) forecast for Kisumu calls for a maximum temperature of 32.0°C / 90°F and minimum of 19.0°C / 66°F with sunny intervals tomorrow and partly cloudy conditions tonight. Kenya Met predicts dry conditions for today and Tuesday (Sept 8), agreeing with the numerical consensus on today's dry call but dissenting from the numerical rain consensus on Day+3. At Day+0, Kenya Met holds an 80% rolling rain verification rate (75% all-time); at Day+3, it holds a 100% verification rate across 9 checks, though its sample size remains small.
Ground AQI station breakdown: All ground AQI stations currently report stale readings from 3 hours ago: Kisumu Airport (AQI 5, PM2.5 5.0 µg/m³, PM10 15.0 µg/m³), Ochieng' Avenue (AQI 55, PM2.5 55.0 µg/m³, PM10 18.0 µg/m³), and Dunga Beach (AQI 57, PM2.5 57.0 µg/m³, PM10 37.0 µg/m³).
Historical notes cross-reference: Yesterday's run (2026-09-04) experienced an unforecasted evening shower despite dry model guidance, reinforcing that high nocturnal CAPE setups in Nyanza Basin regularly produce localized convection even when surface precipitation outputs report 0.0 mm.
